status_legend.ALREADY_COVERED: Neta already has a bounded research/method claim covering the useful distinction; do not create a new rule.
status_legend.WORKFLOW_HEURISTIC: Useful practitioner process guidance, but not evidence of user outcome or universal design truth.
status_legend.RESEARCH_COMPATIBLE_CANDIDATE: Potential residual worth future research after the current holdout wave closes.
status_legend.REJECT_AS_UNIVERSAL: The strong universal wording is contradicted or overbroad; only a narrower conditional form may survive.
status_legend.IMPLEMENTATION_CONVENTION: A technical/design-system convention that may be useful locally but is not a Neta research construct.
status_legend.MEASUREMENT_BOUNDARY: A validated measure can assess a field construct but cannot diagnose the mechanism or prescribe the fix.
status_legend.SOURCE_METHOD: A provenance/independence rule about how evidence is counted, not a frontend design claim.

claims.candidate: Design direction should be grounded in the product's subject matter, audience, task and constraints before stylistic defaults are chosen.
denied_inference: the inferred aesthetic will be preferred by users
the agent can replace OWNER intent
claims.rationale: The practitioner sources converge on brief-first grounding and ISO 9241-110 grounds interaction in user tasks and context. The residual is not whether context matters, but how Neta should operationalize brief-to-visual-world synthesis without laundering taste into field truth.
claims.next_discriminator: Compare whether a candidate visual direction can be traced to explicit product/audience/task evidence versus category-default aesthetics, while holding implementation quality constant.

claims.candidate: The current interface is evidence about product history and constraints, not automatic authority over a redesign.
denied_inference: old UI is wrong because it is old
repo evidence settles owner taste or field preference
claims.rationale: Neta already separates REPO evidence from OWNER and FIELD authority. Impeccable's redesign/refinement distinction is a useful concrete instance, not a new epistemic rule.
claims.next_discriminator: For each redesign request, list confirmed invariants, incumbent-only choices, owner-pinned commitments and unresolved field assumptions before changing the visual world.

claims.candidate: For an existing product, reproduce or faithfully characterize the current rendered target before generating redesign variants.
claims.rationale: This is a strong anti-invention workflow for agents. It is especially valuable when code branches or responsive states differ. It remains process guidance rather than user-outcome evidence.
claims.next_discriminator: Require baseline capture when a redesign claim depends on what currently renders; skip it only when the target is genuinely new or the old surface has no decision authority.

claims.candidate: A control that feels unresponsive should be decomposed into completion latency, acknowledgement, progress uncertainty and state-transition salience.
denied_inference: one timing threshold fits all contexts
claims.rationale: This is already one of Neta's best-supported research distinctions. Practitioner motion guidance adds craft options but does not change the authority boundary.
claims.next_discriminator: Measure acknowledgement and completion separately, then check whether the resulting state is perceptually discoverable.

claims.candidate: Motion should have a state, feedback, spatial-continuity or explanatory purpose rather than being added as decoration by default.
denied_inference: all UI animations must be under one fixed duration
claims.rationale: Purposeful feedback is compatible with existing research and standards, but exact durations and easing recipes remain craft heuristics. Neta should preserve the mechanism and quarantine the recipe.
claims.next_discriminator: Ask what information the motion communicates. If removing it leaves acknowledgement, state and spatial continuity equally legible, treat it as optional craft rather than mechanism.

claims.candidate: Every viewport should expose exactly one primary CTA or action.
denied_inference: multiple visible choices necessarily create overload
claims.rationale: Neta's existing research already falsifies a universal one-action rule. Choice-overload effects are heterogeneous and depend on task, choice complexity, preference uncertainty and user goal. The narrower execution-state version survives.
claims.next_discriminator: Determine whether the user is executing a chosen task or legitimately comparing alternatives. Apply primary-action compression only in the former unless local evidence says otherwise.

claims.candidate: Less content, fewer choices, more whitespace and fewer cards are inherently cognitively better.
claims.rationale: Existing Neta research distinguishes quantity from grouping and extraneous cost from task-relevant value. Reducing content can destroy information scent, comparison value or measurement integrity.
claims.next_discriminator: Hold content constant while changing grouping/rank, then hold structure constant while changing quantity. Remove only what is shown to be extraneous for the live task.

claims.candidate: A 12-column desktop grid, 8px spacing baseline, 1200-1440px content width and similar numeric recipes are professional-design requirements.
denied_inference: violating the number is a UX defect
the recipe generalizes across surfaces, devices or design systems
claims.rationale: These can be useful implementation defaults in a local design system. They are not constructs and should never be promoted merely because a skill phrases them as DO/DON'T rules.
claims.next_discriminator: Prefer the incumbent design system or task-specific layout evidence. Use numeric defaults only when no stronger local authority exists and keep them reversible.

claims.candidate: A design that looks templated or obviously AI-generated is necessarily worse.
denied_inference: anti-slop is an empirical usability scale
claims.rationale: The lineage repeats the concern, but the repetitions are not independent and the claim is aesthetic. Neta's W1-AES-001 already keeps aesthetics, perceived craft, modernity and task usability separable.
claims.next_discriminator: Test whether the complaint changes under a skin-only transformation while task structure stays fixed. If so, keep it as an aesthetic/craft signal rather than relabeling it usability.

claims.candidate: Interface vocabulary should be expressed in the user's task language rather than the system's internal ontology when the two differ.
denied_inference: novice vocabulary should replace expert domain vocabulary
claims.rationale: This aligns strongly with Neta's owner-language philosophy and ISO self-descriptiveness/conformity with user expectations, but it has not yet been isolated as a frontend research claim. The important boundary is novice task-language versus legitimate expert/domain language.
claims.next_discriminator: Compare whether a new user can predict the action/result from the interface term without knowing implementation vocabulary, while preserving expert terms that are part of the user's actual domain.

claims.candidate: When the visual world is genuinely unsettled, generate multiple materially different candidate systems before committing to implementation.
denied_inference: the agent may choose owner taste
claims.rationale: This transfers Neta's competing-mechanism logic into visual synthesis and is operationally attractive. It remains a decision workflow, not evidence that any candidate is better.
claims.next_discriminator: Require variants to differ on a named structural or visual-world hypothesis, not superficial palette swaps; stop when additional variants no longer change the decision.

claims.candidate: A standardized UX score can diagnose which frontend mechanism is wrong and therefore what should be redesigned.
denied_inference: score authorizes a specific design fix
claims.rationale: Validated instruments are valuable because they measure defined field constructs. Their strength is exactly why Neta must not misuse them as mechanism detectors.
claims.next_discriminator: Use the instrument only after defining the field construct and comparison. Diagnose mechanisms with separate observations or experiments.

claims.candidate: Passing WCAG accessibility criteria establishes that the interface is generally usable, understandable and preferred.
denied_inference: WCAG conformance proves aesthetics or preference
accessibility pass settles all FIELD claims
claims.rationale: WCAG is a normative accessibility standard with testable success criteria. Its authority is strong inside that construct and intentionally bounded outside it.
claims.next_discriminator: State the exact success criterion or accessibility claim. Route broader usability/comprehension/preference claims to separate evidence.

claims.candidate: If several popular frontend skills repeat the same rule, the repetition counts as independent corroboration.
denied_inference: a synthesis is independent of its parents
claims.rationale: Impeccable explicitly descends from Anthropic frontend-design; design-taste explicitly synthesizes Impeccable, Emil and taste-skill. Claim-level lineage must be deduplicated before any triangulation count.
claims.next_discriminator: For every imported rule, identify the earliest accessible source and mark derived repetitions as shared lineage unless the later source contributes genuinely independent evidence or a novel mechanism.
